arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Amunson argued that defendants retain the statutory right to appeal a conviction during plea bargaining.
Mr. Feigin contended that Rule 11(a)(2) mandates a conditional plea to preserve statutory challenges.
Justice Ginsburg questioned whether statute of limitations claims fit within the rule's scope.
Justice Alito noted that interlocutory appeals protect certain rights, asking if this applies here.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 11(a)(2). The rule governs how defendants preserve legal challenges while pleading guilty. The core conflict involves the tension between finality and the right to appeal statutory defects.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This issue determines whether defendants can challenge the constitutionality of criminal statutes after pleading guilty. It affects the finality of plea agreements and the scope of appellate review. The outcome shapes the balance between judicial efficiency and individual rights.
